poster_title: MEMTRACK: Evaluating Long-Term Memory and State Tracking in Multi-Platform Dynamic Agent Environments
authors: Darshan Deshpande, Varun Gangal, Hersh Mehta, Anand Kannappan, Rebecca Qian, Peng Wang
paper_info: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Workshop: Scaling Environments for Agents (SEA). arXiv:2510.01353v1 [cs.AI] 1 Oct 2025

content: Context and memory benchmarking focused on conversational instances.
Need for evaluating memory in dynamic enterprise environments.
Memory essential for managing and evolving enterprise components.
Existing benchmarks lack ecological validity for real-world tasks.
Need to evaluate memory over long horizons and across platforms.
Quantitative evaluation of memory retrieval and maintenance is understudied.
MEMTRACK benchmark for long-term memory and state tracking.
Models realistic workflows with asynchronous events across platforms.
Supports brief phrase outputs for evaluation using LLM-as-judge.
Three data curation methodologies: top-down, bottom-up, and hybrid.
Conducted on state-of-the-art LLMs and memory backends.
Dataset contains 47 curated long context datapoints.
Benchmark environment includes asynchronous tools and live servers.
Best GPT-5 model achieves 60% Correctness on MEMTRACK.
LLMs struggle with context retention and repeated information reading.
Memory tools increase redundancy in planning and tool use.
MEMTRACK advances evaluation research for memory-augmented agents.
State-of-the-art models face significant challenges in context reasoning and memory management.
